</ol>
<details class="mcq-why"><summary>Show answer</summary>
<p><strong>C.</strong> 10 MiB matches the image budget, forces pre-summarizing large documents, and inflates to roughly 14 MiB in base64, leaving room for the prompt scaffold under 32 MiB. The cap was not changed during the arc. See §84.2.</p>
</details>
</div>
</div>
<p class="engage-kicker">Problem set</p>
<div class="pset" id="pset-part-xv">
<div class="problem">
<p class="problem-q"><strong>Problem 1 (trace).</strong> An operator types <code>/attach /tmp/claude/bug.png "what is misaligned here?"</code> in SerpentFlow. Trace the file from the REPL to the Claude request, naming each check it passes and the two log lines you could grep for afterwards.</p>
<details class="problem-hint"><summary>Hint</summary>
<p>Follow §83.2, then the hoist in §83.3, then the gates in §84.4 and the block shape in §85.1. The log lines are in §85.4.</p>
</details>
<details class="problem-sol"><summary>Worked solution</summary>
<p><code>SerpentFlow._handle_attach()</code> parses the path and description, then runs the validation perimeter: absolute path, file exists, extension in <code>_ATTACHMENT_EXT_TO_MIME</code>, size within the 10 MiB default, and <code>_is_protected_path(path)</code> returns None (§83.2). It builds an envelope with <code>source="voice_human"</code>, empty <code>target_files</code>, and <code>evidence["user_attachments"]</code>, and calls the intake router's <code>ingest</code>.</p>
<p>In <code>_dispatch</code>, the hoist reads <code>user_attachments</code>, calls <code>Attachment.from_file(path, kind="user_provided")</code>, which computes <code>hash8</code> and infers <code>image/png</code>, and logs <code>[IntakeRouter] attachments_hoisted ... kind=user_provided</code>. The context gets the tuple via <code>with_attachments</code> (§83.3).</p>
<p>At GENERATE, <code>_serialize_attachments()</code> checks the purpose is allowed, the kill switch is on, attachments exist, and the route is not BG or SPEC, then reads the bytes within budget (§84.4). For Claude it emits an image block, and <code>_generate_raw</code> places it before the text block (§85.1). The provider logs <code>[ClaudeProvider] multi_modal op=... blocks=1 ... mime_kinds=[image/png]</code> (§85.4, §90.2). Grepping the op id finds both lines.</p>
</details>
</div>
<div class="problem">
<p class="problem-q"><strong>Problem 2 (design).</strong> A teammate wants to raise the attachment cap to 32 MiB so long PDFs fit, arguing "Anthropic allows it". Using §84.2, §88 and §89.6, argue for or against, and suggest a better path for long documents.</p>
<details class="problem-hint"><summary>Hint</summary>
<p>Consider base64 inflation, the prompt scaffold, and what §88 says about relaxing gates.</p>
</details>
<details class="problem-sol"><summary>Worked solution</summary>
<p>Against. At 10 MiB the base64 payload is about 14 MiB, leaving headroom under Anthropic's 32 MiB limit for system text and tool manifests (§84.2). A 32 MiB file would inflate well past 32 MiB and risk a payload-oversize 400.</p>
<p>The paper also treats the cap as a hard gate. It says relaxing a safety budget to fit a new code path is the anti-pattern that Manifesto §6 forbids, and §88 confirms none of the gates were relaxed.</p>
<p>Even within the cap, §89.6 notes that a long PDF sent as one block can push token counts above the context window. The better path is the future work it describes: per-page extraction with page-range arguments to <code>/attach</code>, or operators pre-summarizing large documents, which the cap already encourages.</p>
</details>
</div>
<div class="problem">
<p class="problem-q"><strong>Problem 3 (code reading).</strong> Open <code>backend/core/ouroboros/governance/providers.py</code> and find <code>_serialize_attachments</code> (search for <code>_ATTACHMENT_PURPOSES_ALLOWED</code>). List the early-return checks in the order they appear, and compare them with the five gates named in §84.4. Is there a check in the code that the paper's list does not name?</p>
<details class="problem-hint"><summary>Hint</summary>
<p>Read from the line <code>if purpose not in _ATTACHMENT_PURPOSES_ALLOWED</code> down to where the <code>blocks</code> list is created.</p>
</details>
<details class="problem-sol"><summary>Worked solution</summary>
<p>The function returns an empty list, in order, when: the purpose is not in <code>_ATTACHMENT_PURPOSES_ALLOWED</code> (which holds <code>sensor_classify</code>, <code>visual_verify</code> and <code>generate</code>); the purpose is <code>generate</code> and <code>_generate_attachments_enabled()</code> is false; <code>ctx.attachments</code> is empty; the route is in <code>_ATTACHMENT_STRIPPED_ROUTES</code>; and the provider kind is not in <code>_ATTACHMENT_PROVIDER_KINDS</code>.</p>
<p>The first four match §84.4's known-purpose, env-kill, non-empty ctx and live-route gates. The fifth paper gate, the per-attachment read budget, happens later inside the loop when bytes are read.</p>
<p>The unknown-provider-kind check is in the code but not in the paper's list of five. It logs at DEBUG and drops all attachments for a provider that is not Claude, DoubleWord or J-Prime.</p>
<p>One more drift is worth noticing: the function's docstring still says purpose must be <code>sensor_classify</code> or <code>visual_verify</code>, while the allow-list constant includes <code>generate</code>. The constant is what runs.</p>
</details>
</div>
</div>
<p class="engage-kicker engage-kicker-adv">Advanced conceptual questions</p>
<details class="cq-adv"><summary>A1. §91 claims "true CC-parity" for seeing a screenshot of a bug. The proof in §87 ran on Claude. Under the October configuration in §93.6, which parts of that claim still hold, and what live test would re-establish it?</summary>
<p>The intake half still holds, because it does not depend on the provider. Both ingress paths still converge on <code>ctx.attachments</code> (§83), and the hoist, the Attachment schema and the five gates do not change with the lane. The provider half is different. With <code>JARVIS_PAID_LANES_ENABLED=false</code>, Claude is never constructed (§93.6), so the <code>document</code> and <code>image</code> blocks of §85.1 are never sent.</p>
<p>The only active lane is J-Prime. For <code>jprime</code> the serializer emits OpenAI-style <code>image_url</code> blocks and drops PDFs with a WARNING (§85.2, §89.5). So a PDF attached today is dropped, and the op runs text-only. The §85.2 escape hatch, <code>JARVIS_PROVIDER_OVERRIDE=claude-api</code>, names a provider the paid-lane authority keeps switched off.</p>
<p>Images are the open case. They would be sent, but the model serving code generation is <code>qwen3-coder-ov:30b</code>, and §93.6 says the vision model (<code>jarvis-vision:8b</code>) is declared in J-Prime but at the time of writing is still partly served by Ollama. The paper gives no live-fire proof that the local lane reasons over image bytes at GENERATE.</p>
<p>So in October the parity claim holds for the architecture and is unproven for behaviour. The test that would settle it is the §87 method on the local lane: an image with a unique, unguessable string, run through <code>scripts/attach_livefire.py</code>, passing only if the reply quotes the string verbatim. It would also need both breadcrumbs from §85.4 under one <code>op_id</code>. Note that the §85.4 line is labelled <code>[ClaudeProvider]</code>, so the breadcrumb to grep for may differ on J-Prime.</p>
</details>
<details class="cq-adv"><summary>A2. The intake hoist fails closed by demoting a broken attachment op to text-only, logged at DEBUG (§83.3). §93.12 later added capability assurance, which refuses to run below the declared envelope instead of degrading silently. Should an <code>/attach</code> op whose file vanished still run? Argue it per kind.</summary>
<p>The two principles conflict here. §83.3 chose availability: a stale frame, a deleted file or a failed mime check must not break intake, so the op still enters CLASSIFY without pixels. §93.12's capability assurance chose honesty: an operation should not run with less than it declared it needs.</p>
<p>My position (a proposal, not described in the paper) is to decide by kind. For <code>sensor_frame</code>, demotion is right. The useful signal has already been pulled out at the sensor: OCR text, the Tier-1 verdict and the matches travel in <code>evidence["vision_signal"]</code> (§83.1). A text-only op can still act on "a traceback is on screen", and Ferrari may have died between scan and intake (§89.1).</p>
<p>For <code>user_provided</code>, demotion is misleading. The operator asked something like "what is misaligned here?" about a specific file (§90.2). Without the image the model answers a different question, and the operator has no visible sign of it because the only trace is a DEBUG line. That is the silent degradation §93.12 exists to refuse. The better behaviour is to fail the op visibly back to the REPL.</p>
<p>The evidence to settle it is already in the logs. Using the §90.3 grep rollup, count envelopes that carried <code>user_attachments</code> but have no matching <code>attachments_hoisted</code> line, and check whether their answers referred to the missing content. If that count is near zero, the question is academic. If not, the per-kind split matters.</p>
</details>
<details class="cq-adv"><summary>A3. The multi-modal arc needed five contract fixes before one signal could be emitted (§82.2), even though every component existed. Connect this to §87's live-fire method and §93.12's DARK-feature finding. What general rule about proof does the paper end up adopting?</summary>
<p>Every component in §82.1 worked on its own terms. The frame server wrote frames, the sensor scanned, the serializer could encode blocks. Each producer and consumer pair disagreed on one detail: the filename, the timestamp key, the hash format, a missing <code>ocr_fn</code>, and a purpose allow-list without <code>"generate"</code>. Each mismatch failed silently, for example <code>ferrari_absent</code> every 60 s while Ferrari was healthy, or <code>no_regex_match ocr_chars=0</code>. Unit tests on either side would pass, because each side matched its own idea of the contract.</p>
<p>§87 answers this with an end-to-end behavioural test. Real bytes go to the real API, and the test passes only if the reply contains a string that could not have been guessed. No single-side test can pass that check by agreeing with itself.</p>
<p>§93.12 shows the same pattern at system scale: 131 features with the flag on, the module present, and no production caller. The reachability ledger's three stages (registered, invoked, effective) apply §82.2's lesson to every feature. The arc's own unblocking step was the same idea in small form: commit <code>44305f7e96</code> instrumented the silent-skip paths before deeper debugging (§88).</p>
<p>The general rule is that a capability counts as present only when a live run shows it being invoked and having its effect. Having the code, the flag and the unit tests is not enough. §93.10's "first-order proof" applies the same standard to commits: an autonomous landing counts only when it did real work for a signed goal and git confirms it.</p>
</details>
<p class="engage-kicker engage-kicker-adv">Challenge problems</p>
<div class="pset pset-adv">
<div class="problem problem-adv">
<p class="problem-q"><strong>Challenge 1 (adversarial).</strong> §83.2 says <code>/attach</code> reuses Venom's <code>_is_protected_path()</code> as step 5 of its validation perimeter. Write an envelope that gets a file inside a protected location sent to a provider at GENERATE without going through that check. You may use any producer the paper shows calling <code>router.ingest</code>. Identify every gate it passes, and say whether anything in the paper's design stops it. (Reference: the hoist is in <code>backend/core/ouroboros/governance/intake/unified_intake_router.py</code>, and <code>Attachment.from_file</code> is in <code>backend/core/ouroboros/governance/op_context.py</code>.)</p>
<details class="problem-hint"><summary>Hint</summary>
<p>Compare where the protected-path check runs (§83.2) with where the hoist builds Attachments (§83.3). §87.2 shows a producer that builds the envelope itself.</p>
</details>
<details class="problem-sol"><summary>Worked solution</summary>
<p><strong>Where the check lives.</strong> In §83.2, the protected-path check is step 5 inside <code>SerpentFlow._handle_attach()</code>, at the REPL edge. The hoist in §83.3 reads <code>evidence["user_attachments"]</code> and calls <code>Attachment.from_file(path, kind="user_provided")</code> directly. In the repo, the hoist in <code>unified_intake_router.py</code> calls <code>from_file</code> with no protected-path call, and <code>from_file</code> in <code>op_context.py</code> checks only for a non-empty absolute path, that the file exists, and that the extension is whitelisted. A search finds no <code>_is_protected_path</code> call in the intake router.</p>
<p><strong>The envelope.</strong> §87.2 shows <code>scripts/attach_livefire.py</code> building an <code>IntentEnvelope</code> with <code>make_envelope()</code> and calling <code>router.ingest()</code> itself, with no REPL. Any in-process producer can do the same, including a future ingress like the Slack webhook §83.4 anticipates. Give it <code>source="voice_human"</code>, <code>urgency="critical"</code>, empty <code>target_files</code> (allowed because <code>user_attachments</code> is present, §86 commit 12c), and one entry whose path is an absolute path under a protected directory with a <code>.png</code> or <code>.pdf</code> extension and a size of 10 MiB or less.</p>
<p><strong>Gates it passes.</strong> At the hoist: absolute path, file exists, whitelisted extension, mime inferred from the extension, and <code>hash8</code> computed from the bytes. In <code>__post_init__</code>: kind, mime, hash format and path length are all valid (§84.1). In the serializer (§84.4): the purpose is <code>generate</code>, the kill switch is on by default, the context is non-empty, and the route is IMMEDIATE, not BG or SPEC (critical plus voice_human, §87.5). The per-attachment read is within 10 MiB. Then the bytes are base64-encoded and sent.</p>
<p><strong>What stops it.</strong> Nothing in the paper's design, for any file that has a whitelisted extension. The extension whitelist does narrow the target: a file such as <code>.env</code> has no whitelisted extension, so <code>from_file</code> raises and the hoist demotes the op to text-only. Note also that the mime type comes from the extension, not from the file's content, so any bytes renamed to <code>.png</code> pass the schema.</p>
<p>A proposed fix (not in the paper): run <code>_is_protected_path()</code> inside the hoist or inside <code>from_file</code> for <code>user_provided</code>, so every ingress inherits the check. This matches §83.4's own rule that new ingresses only add a <code>kind</code> at the hoist. Today a new ingress would have to remember to call the check itself. Check your answer by asking which layer is reached by every producer: only the hoist is.</p>
</details>
</div>
<div class="problem problem-adv">
<p class="problem-q"><strong>Challenge 2 (quantitative).</strong> §84.1 allows up to 8 attachments per context (<code>_ATTACHMENT_MAX_PER_CTX</code>), and each may be up to 10 MiB. §84.2 says 10 MiB inflates to about 14 MiB of base64, "well below" the 32 MiB Anthropic limit. Compute the worst-case payload for a full context, find the largest number of maximum-size attachments that still fits under 32 MiB, and say which of the five gates in §84.4 would stop an oversize request. What happens if a ninth attachment is supplied?</p>
<details class="problem-hint"><summary>Hint</summary>
<p>Base64 turns every 3 bytes into 4. Check whether any gate in §84.4 looks at the total across attachments.</p>
</details>
<details class="problem-sol"><summary>Worked solution</summary>
<p><strong>Per attachment.</strong> 10 MiB x 4/3 = about 13.3 MiB of base64. The paper rounds this to about 14 MiB.</p>
<p><strong>Full context.</strong> 8 x 13.3 = about 107 MiB (8 x 14 = 112 MiB with the paper's rounding), before any prompt scaffold. That is more than three times the 32 MiB figure.</p>
<p><strong>Largest set that fits.</strong> Two maximum-size attachments are about 26.7 MiB, leaving about 5.3 MiB for the system text and tool manifests. Three are about 40 MiB, which is over the limit. So the safety margin in §84.2 holds for one attachment, and roughly for two. From three upwards it does not.</p>
<p><strong>Which gate stops it.</strong> None of the five. Known-purpose, env-kill, non-empty context and live-route are all yes/no checks. The read budget is per attachment: each file is read with the 10 MiB cap, and in the repo <code>_serialize_attachments</code> in <code>providers.py</code> calls <code>att.read_bytes()</code> for each attachment without any running total. The 8-per-context cap counts attachments, not bytes. So a three-attachment op reaches the provider and risks exactly the payload-oversize 400 that §84.2 says the budget is meant to avoid.</p>
<p><strong>A ninth attachment.</strong> In <code>op_context.py</code>, <code>with_attachments</code> raises if there are more than <code>_ATTACHMENT_MAX_PER_CTX</code> entries. The hoist wraps everything in one try/except (§83.3), so the whole hoist fails and the op runs with zero attachments, not eight. A request over the count limit loses everything, while a request over the byte limit is sent anyway.</p>
<p>A proposed fix (not in the paper): add an aggregate byte budget in the serializer, derived from the provider's payload limit minus a scaffold reserve. Over budget, drop the later attachments with a WARNING, which matches §88's rule that a violating attachment is "dropped at the nearest boundary with a WARNING log". Check: 2 x 10 MiB x 4/3 = 26.7 MiB is less than 32, and 3 x 10 x 4/3 = 40 is more.</p>
</details>
</div>
</div>
<p class="engage-kicker engage-kicker-x">Connections</p>
<div class="pset pset-x">
<div class="problem problem-x">
<p class="problem-q"><strong>Connection 1 (Probability and combinatorics).</strong> An attachment's identity is <code>hash8 = sha256(image_bytes)[:8]</code>: eight hex characters (§82.1, §84.1). §85.4 says the <code>hash8s</code> log field gives "per-attachment identity for cross-op dedup analysis." Treat the truncated SHA-256 output as uniformly random. (a) How many distinct values can <code>hash8</code> take? (b) What is the chance of at least one collision among the 8 attachments a single context may hold (<code>_ATTACHMENT_MAX_PER_CTX</code>)? (c) What is the chance among 1,000, 10,000 and 100,000 distinct attachments collected across many sessions, and at about what count does it reach 50%? (d) The VisionSensor's <code>frame_hash</code> is a 64-bit dhash. Does the same birthday arithmetic describe how its dedup can go wrong?</p>
<details class="problem-hint"><summary>Hint</summary>
<p>Birthday approximation: P(collision among n) is about 1 - exp(-n(n-1) / (2N)), where N is the number of possible values. The 50% point is at n of about sqrt(2N ln 2).</p>
</details>
<details class="problem-sol"><summary>Worked solution</summary>
<p>(a) Eight hex characters carry 8 x 4 = 32 bits, so N = 2^32 = 4,294,967,296 values.</p>
<p>(b) 8 attachments form 8 x 7 / 2 = 28 pairs. P is about 28 / 2^32 = about 6.5 x 10^-9. Within one op, a collision is negligible.</p>
<p>(c) n = 1,000: 499,500 pairs / N = 1.16 x 10^-4, so P is about 0.012%. n = 10,000: 49,995,000 / N = 0.0116, so P = 1 - e^(-0.0116) = about 1.2%. n = 100,000: 4,999,950,000 / N = 1.164, so P = 1 - e^(-1.164) = about 69%. The 50% point is sqrt(2 x 2^32 x 0.693) = sqrt(5.95 x 10^9) = about 77,000 attachments.</p>
<p>So <code>hash8</code> is a good label inside a session log, where it is always paired with an <code>op_id</code> (§85.4). Across a long history of tens of thousands of frames, a matching <code>hash8</code> is evidence that two attachments are the same, not proof; the full SHA-256 is needed for that. Uniformity gives no protection against deliberate collisions either. A second file matching a given <code>hash8</code> needs about 2^32 attempts on average, far fewer than for the full 256-bit hash.</p>
<p>(d) No. A dhash is a perceptual hash: frames that look almost the same are meant to produce the same value. That is the point of Tier 0 dedup (§83.1). Its errors come from the image, not from chance: two meaningfully different screens can hash alike if the difference is small, for example a single changed line of text. The birthday bound describes accidental collisions of a uniform hash. It says nothing about a hash designed to collide on similar inputs. The two hashes do different jobs, identity and similarity, and they need different error analyses.</p>
</details>
</div>
<div class="problem problem-x">
<p class="problem-q"><strong>Connection 2 (Queueing theory).</strong> Ferrari captures the display at about 15 fps (§82.1). The OCR adapter in Accurate mode takes about 130 ms warm and about 700 ms cold on Apple Silicon (§89.2). VisionSensor does not process every frame. It polls asynchronously with an adaptive 1 to 8 s throttle, and Tier 0 dedups by dhash before OCR runs (§83.1). Assume OCR runs on one worker, one frame at a time, and dominates the per-scan cost. (a) Compute the OCR utilization ρ = λS if every captured frame were OCR'd, warm and cold. (b) Compute ρ at the 1 s and 8 s poll intervals, in the worst case where every poll reaches OCR. (c) Use Little's law to find the average number of OCR jobs in progress at a 1 s poll. (d) What does this say about the design and about Fast mode?</p>
<details class="problem-hint"><summary>Hint</summary>
<p>A single-server queue is stable only if ρ is below 1. The maximum throughput of the worker is 1/S.</p>
</details>
<details class="problem-sol"><summary>Worked solution</summary>
<p>(a) λ = 15 frames/s. Warm: ρ = 15 x 0.13 = 1.95. Cold: ρ = 15 x 0.7 = 10.5. Both exceed 1. The worker can finish at most 1/0.13 = about 7.7 frames/s warm, so a backlog would grow without bound and OCR results would describe screens that no longer exist.</p>
<p>(b) At a 1 s poll, λ = 1/s. Warm ρ = 0.13, cold ρ = 0.7. At an 8 s poll, λ = 0.125/s and warm ρ = 0.125 x 0.13 = about 0.016. These are upper bounds: dedup and the app denylist stop many polls before OCR, so real utilization is lower.</p>
<p>(c) Little's law: L = λW. With λ = 1/s and W of about 0.13 s (no queueing at this utilization), L = 0.13. On average the OCR worker is busy 13% of the time and idle the rest.</p>
<p>(d) Separating the sampling rate from the capture rate turns an unstable queue into a lightly loaded one. Capture can run at 15 fps for freshness, while the expensive stage runs at most once per second. The dhash dedup ensures that a static screen is OCR'd only once. Because the 1 s rate is so far below capacity, Accurate mode's extra cost is affordable. That supports §89.2's choice of Accurate as the default: Fast mode would save CPU the system is not short of, at the cost of dropping the top lines of a sparse traceback, exactly the text the Tier-1 regex needs (§82.2). The proposed adaptive Fast/Accurate selection would matter only if the poll rate rose towards the 1/S limit, or if a cold start (ρ = 0.7 at 1 s) persisted.</p>
</details>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<!-- engage:end -->

## §92. Recent Developments (April 17 – May 13, 2026)

> **Big Picture.** The original 2026-04-16 stamp captured O+V as a system that had just proven end-to-end autonomous APPLY (Session W, 2026-04-15). The four weeks since have been a transition from *proving capability exists* to *graduating capability into the default-on substrate, and adding the operator-visible surface layer that makes a proactive system legible.* No claim in §1–§91 has been retracted; the additions below extend rather than amend the substrate. The same audit-trail discipline applies — every arc cited here has a regression test count, a graduation date, and a memory-file under `memory/project_*.md`.

This addendum is intentionally dense: the four-week window covers ~40 distinct shipping events, including the **closure of the last structural-engineering arc** on the §35 / §3.6.3 / §37 PRD tables (2026-05-09) and the **start of the Phase 9 flag-graduation cadence** (2026-05-05). It is grouped thematically rather than chronologically; per-arc detail lives in the indexed memory files.

---

### §92.1 Phase B Subagent Family — Graduated Default-True (2026-04-20)

All four Phase B subagents shipped to default-on in a single day, with 138 regression tests green at arc close:

- **EXPLORE** — read-only context-expansion subagent.
- **REVIEW** — pre-APPLY semantic critique under `JARVIS_REVIEW_SUBAGENT_SHADOW=true` (shadow-mode by default).
- **PLAN** — parallel-edge planning shadow + default-on. Multi-file ops measured at ~4× wall-clock speedup.
- **GENERAL** — infrastructure-only subagent gated by the **Semantic Firewall** (`semantic_firewall.py`): 11 injection detectors, 5 credential shapes, recursion ban, output quarantine fence, hard-kill wrapper. Paired with the **mutation cage** (`scoped_tool_backend.py`) — per-instance mutation counter + budget as a structural COUNT gate (second-rejection after the type gate, `POLICY_DENIED reason=mutation_budget_exhausted`). The `state_mirror` dict preserves `exec_trace` across hard-kill so the audit survives the cage. LLM driver master flag `JARVIS_GENERAL_LLM_DRIVER_ENABLED` graduated default-TRUE.

Phase C Slices 1a+1b + Epochs 1+2 landed the same day. Detail: `memory/project_phase_b_subagent_roadmap.md`, `project_phase_c_general_llm_driver.md`.

### §92.2 Sensor Event-Primary Campaign + IDE Observability Surface (2026-04-20)

**Gap #4** closed: 9 of 13 sensors are now event-primary, 4 retained on polling by design (RuntimeHealth, WebIntelligence, ProactiveExploration, Scheduled — architectural, not deferred). Webhook transport for GitHub/CI; `TrinityEventBus` `fs.changed.*` for filesystem sensors (TestFailure, TodoScanner, Backlog, OpportunityMiner) with a layered storm-guard; conversation-bus for IntentDiscovery. The `EventChannelServer` exposes multi-surface (`/webhook/github`, `/webhook/ci`) and per-sensor telemetry on `/channel/health`. ~120 tests.

The **IDE Observability** surface (Gap #6) graduated the same day across two slices:

<p class="qc-label">Quick check · §92.2</p>
<details class="qc"><summary>1. Four sensors (RuntimeHealth, WebIntelligence, ProactiveExploration, Scheduled) stayed on polling. Is that unfinished migration?</summary>

<details class="qc"><summary>3. The SSE stream is bounded (8 subscribers × 64 queue × 512 history) and drops the oldest events. Why bound it, and why send a single <code>stream_lag</code> event?</summary>
<p>Without bounds, a slow or stuck client could make the organism buffer without limit. Dropping the oldest event protects the server. The <code>stream_lag</code> event tells the client it missed events, so it can resync with <code>Last-Event-ID</code> replay from the 512-event history instead of silently showing a wrong picture.</p>
</details>
</div>

<div class="quick-check" id="qc-92-3">
<p class="qc-label">Quick check · §92.3</p>
<details class="qc"><summary>1. <code>PostureObserver</code> runs every 300 s but applies 900 s of hysteresis. What does the hysteresis buy?</summary>
<p>It stops the posture from flapping between values on every noisy reading. A new posture has to persist well beyond one observation before it takes over. The 0.75 confidence bypass lets a strong, unambiguous signal switch sooner, and operator overrides are clamped to 24 h so they cannot linger forever.</p>
</details>
<details class="qc"><summary>2. The SensorGovernor's emergency brake fires on <code>cost_burn&gt;0.9</code> OR <code>postmortem_rate&gt;0.6</code>. Why OR rather than AND?</summary>
<p>Each condition is dangerous on its own. Spend running away is a reason to slow down even if ops succeed, and a high postmortem rate is a reason to slow down even if it is cheap. Requiring both would let a cheap failure loop, or an expensive successful one, run at full rate. Either trigger drops caps to 20%.</p>
</details>
<details class="qc"><summary>3. Why does a registry of 481+ <code>JARVIS_*</code> flags need typo detection?</summary>
<p>An environment variable with a misspelled name is simply ignored, so the operator believes a feature is on or off when it is not. Bounded Levenshtein matching turns <code>JARVIS_POSTUR_ENABLED</code> into a suggestion of <code>JARVIS_POSTURE_ENABLED</code>, so the silent failure becomes visible.</p>
</details>
</div>
<!-- engage:end -->

<p class="cp-q">One battle-test session hung in GENERATE for over an hour because provider retry storms kept resetting the per-op idle counter. What kind of guard would stop this, and what signal must that guard refuse to listen to?</p>

Graduation soaks now set it, typically to 2400 s, about twice the 850–1300 s happy path. See §92.4.</p>
</details>

### §92.4 Battle-Test Harness Hardening + Adversarial Cage (2026-04-23 / 2026-04-27)

The harness (`battle_test/harness.py`) gained three structural guards on 2026-04-23 (Wave 2 / Tickets A1+B+C):

- **`--max-wall-seconds`** (env `OUROBOROS_BATTLE_MAX_WALL_SECONDS`): hard wall-clock ceiling, fires `stop_reason=wall_clock_cap` when exceeded. Opaque to any activity signal so it cannot be defeated by provider retry storms that reset the per-op liveness counter — the exact failure mode that hung session #7 GENERATE S2 for 67+ min. Graduation soaks now set this (typical 2400s for ~2× safety margin over the 850–1300s happy-path).
- **`--headless`** (env `OUROBOROS_BATTLE_HEADLESS`): skips the `SerpentREPL` input task. Agent-conducted soaks, CI, and daemons set this (or rely on auto-detect via `not sys.stdin.isatty()`). Replaces the deprecated `tail -f /dev/null | python3 ...` stdin-guard idiom.
- **Signal handling**: SIGHUP / SIGINT / SIGTERM install handlers + SIGPIPE is ignored. On any of those signals the harness writes a partial `summary.json` with `session_outcome=incomplete_kill` + signal-specific `stop_reason` before the shutdown event fires. Schema is v1.1b (additive — `schema_version` stays 2). Closes the failure class where externally-killed sessions left only `debug.log` and no auditable artifact.

The **Adversarial Cage** (Phase 9.4) landed 2026-04-27: **0/38 escapes, 12/38 documented gaps**. The cage exercises the Iron Gate + Semantic Guardian + Anti-Venom recursion-bound against 38 hand-authored adversarial inputs (prompt injection, recursion attempts, credential exfiltration shapes, AST evasion via Unicode confusables, etc.). Zero escapes — the documented gaps are predicted detection-gaps, not active vulnerabilities. The §35 #2 / §3.6.3 #2 stale-row sync shipped alongside (`memory/project_section_37_tier1_3_ledger_flock.md`).

<div class="quick-check" id="qc-92-5">
<p class="qc-label">Quick check · §92.5</p>
<details class="qc"><summary>1. Why did the status line never appear before the TTY-gate fix?</summary>
<p><code>should_render()</code> asked <code>sys.stdout.isatty()</code>. Under <code>patch_stdout(raw=True)</code>, <code>sys.stdout</code> is a patched stand-in that does not report a TTY, so the check always failed. The fix asks <code>sys.__stdout__</code>, the unpatched original stream.</p>
</details>
<details class="qc"><summary>2. Tool bodies, diffs and op blocks get monotonic refs (<code>t-N</code>, <code>d-N</code>, <code>o-N</code>) that are never reused, even after drop-oldest eviction. What would reuse break?</summary>
<p>A ref the operator saw earlier could silently point to a different artifact after eviction, so <code>/expand t-12</code> might show the wrong thing. With no reuse, an old ref either resolves to its original artifact or to nothing. The prefix also lets one <code>/expand</code> verb route to the right store.</p>
</details>
<details class="qc"><summary>3. The "I'm going to do X" intent prose comes from a fire-and-forget LLM call with a 50-token cap, a 5 s timeout and hard-fail-silent behaviour. Why all three limits?</summary>
<p>Narration exists to make the organism legible, and it must never slow or break the operation it describes. The call is small, short and allowed to fail without a trace. For the per-tool "why" line the channel uses a deterministic descriptor table with no LLM cost at all.</p>
</details>
</div>
<!-- engage:end -->

- **Layer 3** — `JARVIS_TOPOLOGY_SENTINEL_ENABLED` defaults FALSE → v1 yaml `dw_allowed:false` blanket-blocks DW. The YAML was purposely purged in Phase 12 Slice E but the sentinel-flag gate was never set in cadence path.
- **Layer 4** — `httpx 0.28+` requires `socksio` when parent has a `socks5h://` tunnel. First attempt stripped the proxy and broke DNS — the correct structural fix is to **install** `socksio`, not strip the proxy. Pinned `socksio==1.0.0` in `requirements.txt`.

All four fixes preserve operator-override discipline, use portable bash, and compose existing canonical primitives. Layer 5 (topology blanket-block under load — 75% block rate even with all four Layer 1–4 fixes) and Layer 6 (0-cost session-id linkage failure → outcome=infra session=unknown when battle-test wall-clock cap hits before atexit writes summary.json) were deferred to fresh-eyes investigation (v2.87 + v2.88 — both subsequently closed). Detail: `memory/project_v2_86_cadence_connectivity.md`.

### §92.12 Open Questions — The MSE-AI Direction

The four-week window covered here closes the *engineering* arc: the substrate is now both behaviorally proven (Sessions A–W in §42–§47) and structurally graduated (Phase 9 cadence in §92.9). What remains open is the *formal* arc — converting the empirical claims of §1–§91 into mathematically proven theorems. Specifically:

1. **Iron Gate determinism** (§22) is empirically zero-escape across 38 adversarial inputs (§92.4) — the open question is whether this can be proven as a formal property of the AST-validation operator over the space of generated patches, in the framework of certifiably robust networks (Wong et al., PRECISE).
2. **Anti-Venom recursion-bound** (§30) is empirically stable across the L2 / L3 / GENERAL composition — the open question is whether the bounded-RSI claim can be formalized against Wang's Markov-chain RSI formulation (`arXiv:1805.06610`), extended into the non-stationary, multi-repository, memory-augmented setting that O+V actually inhabits.
3. **Reverse Russian Doll containment** (§3, §50) is empirically intact across the four-week window — the open question is whether the thermodynamic-entropy formulation in the working dissertation thesis can be formalized as a sufficient condition for bounded RSI, against the SICA pattern (ICLR 2025, `arXiv:2504.15228`) and the Anthropic ASL-4 safeguard framework.

These three are the substantive open questions the engineering substrate now demands. They are the gap that the MSE-AI program is positioned to close — and the gap that this paper, with §92, brings up to current state.

The remaining subsections (§92.13–§92.18) go deeper on the two load-bearing citation→implementation closures of the window (Treefinement L2 and the SWE-Bench-Pro evaluation arc), name the meta-pattern that emerged, map the five research threads onto specific O+V primitives, sketch the formal direction the working dissertation is developing, and frame the four-week window in the Ten Orders of Trinity Evolution.

### §92.13 Treefinement L2 — The First §40.7 Citation → Implementation Closure (2026-05-11 → 2026-05-12)

> **Big Picture.** The previous L2 self-repair FSM (§52) was linear — five sequential repair iterations under a 120-second timebox, each iteration conditioned only on its predecessor's failure. When iteration N took a wrong fix-strategy turn, iterations N+1..5 inherited the misclassification and the timebox burned out on a dead branch. Empirically the same failure mode that **AlphaVerus** (Vermouth et al., CMU L3 lab, *arXiv:2412.06176*) introduced "treefinement" to address. The Treefinement L2 arc ports that published pattern into O+V's repair pipeline as the first structured citation→implementation closure under PRD §40.7's template.

**The AlphaVerus delta — what was structurally ported.** AlphaVerus's three-step framework (*exploration → treefinement → critique*) maps directly onto O+V's L2 path:

| AlphaVerus phase | O+V implementation |
|---|---|
| **Exploration** — translates programs using verifier feedback | Iron Gate exploration-first discipline + `ExplorationLedger` diversity-weighted scoring (§54) |
| **Treefinement** — iteratively fixes errors guided by verifier feedback + tree search | `RepairTreeRunner` BFS/BEAM_K layer dispatch with cross-branch learning (the published delta over naive parallel repair) |
| **Critique** — validates and filters underspecified/incorrect translations | `CanonicalBranchValidator` composing `ASCIIStrictGate` + `SemanticGuardian.inspect_batch` + `TestRunner.run` per branch |

Tree-search forks at each repair attempt; validator feedback prunes losing branches; surviving branches inform the next layer's GENERATE prompt — the cross-branch learning signal is the actual structural delta over O+V's pre-existing parallel-generator (§M9).

**v3.3 — The substrate (six-phase arc, 2026-05-11):**

| Phase | Scope | Commit | Tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Substrate (taxonomies + dataclasses + budget knobs + flag seed) | `00c7944739` | 40 |
| 1 | Tree runner core (BFS layer dispatch + budget + posture-K) | `271c43a24e` | 42 |
| 2 | Validator integration + pruning | `271c43a24e` | 32 |
| 3 | Cross-branch learning (the AlphaVerus delta) | `d62e5218d1` | 34 |
| 4 | Surfaces (REPL + IDE GET + SSE + `/expand b-N` + persistence) | `28fce98d4f` | 68 |
| 5 | Hardening + integration (strategy gate + 12 AST pins + defense-in-depth) | (in-session) | 27 |

Cumulative substrate: **4 files** (`repair_tree.py` + `repair_tree_archive.py` + `repair_tree_repl.py` + edits to `repair_engine.py`, `serpent_flow.py`, `ide_observability.py`, `ide_observability_stream.py`) / **6,114+ LOC** / **243 regression tests** / **12 consolidated AST pins** / **19 FlagRegistry seeds** / **4 SSE events** / **3 IDE GET routes** / **5-subcommand REPL verb**.

**v3.4 — Production wiring (six-phase A→F arc, 2026-05-12).** v3.3's Phase 5 strategy gate was structurally REACHABLE but BEHAVIORALLY a no-op — no production factory was registered. v3.4 ships the factory + adapter + lazy boot wiring so the gate becomes operationally reachable end-to-end:

| Phase | Scope | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| A | `RepairEngine._generate_repair_candidate` primitive extracted (sha256 bytes-pin re-locked at `9e881fdde25ec5b1`) | 11 |
| B | `GitApplyDiffApplier` — production `DiffApplier` impl via `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` (safe arg-list API, no shell); 5-stage discipline; 8 structured error codes | 27 |
| C | `ProductionBranchGenerator` — composes Phase A primitive + Phase 3 `maybe_inject_sibling_outcomes` cross-branch substrate | 26 |
| D | `production_tree_runner_factory` — pure-function `tree_result_to_repair_result` over closed `LayerVerdict × BranchOutcome` taxonomies | 20 |
| E | `register_production_factory_at_boot` lazy registration; 8 AST pins; 14 defense-in-depth tests (lazy-registration semantics / partial-worktree-failure isolation / git-timeout integration / cancellation through production wiring / master-FALSE keeps registration dormant) | 23 |
| F | PRD update + memory artifact + soak-readiness checklist (documentation only) | 0 |

Cumulative production wiring: **1 new substrate file** (`repair_tree_production.py` ~1,700 LOC) + edits to `repair_engine.py` / **107 new regression tests** / **8 production-wiring AST pins** / **2 new FlagRegistry seeds** / **0 changes to `_run_inner` source bytes** (sha256 still `9e881fdde25ec5b1`).

**Composition discipline — load-bearing.** Tree mode composes **seven canonical surfaces** without duplicating any:

- `WorktreeManager.create()` — COW git worktree, reap-orphans on boot (§80)
- `GitApplyDiffApplier` (Phase B) — the **only** `git apply` subprocess invocation in the codebase, AST-pinned
- `TestRunner.run` — pytest invocation (§64)
- `SemanticGuardian.inspect_batch` — 10 deterministic detectors (§29)
- `CanonicalBranchValidator` — per-branch pruning oracle
- `ProductionBranchGenerator` — provider invocation composing Phase A primitive + Phase 3 cross-branch substrate
- `RepairTreeRunner` — BFS/BEAM_K layer dispatch

Composition over fork is the structural answer to AlphaVerus's open question of *how* treefinement integrates into an existing repair pipeline without forking the substrate.

**§1 Boundary preserved.** `repair_tree_production.py` MUST NOT import `orchestrator`, `iron_gate`, `change_engine`, `candidate_generator`, `policy_engine`, or `risk_tier` — AST-pinned. `repair_engine.py` MUST NOT have a top-level import of `repair_tree_production` — lazy import inside `_invoke_tree_factory` only (circular-import safety + zero-cost for non-tree-mode callers).

**Phase 9 graduation criterion.** Master flag `JARVIS_L2_TREEFINEMENT_ENABLED` stays default-FALSE until 3-clean-soak ladder demonstrates **≥10% L2 success-rate lift OR ≥20% wall-clock reduction** at parity success rate over ≥2 consecutive soaks. Empirically derived, no hand-tuning. Production-factory wiring is the prerequisite for graduation soaks. Rollback: `JARVIS_L2_BRANCHING_STRATEGY=linear` (immediate fall-through) OR `JARVIS_L2_TREEFINEMENT_ENABLED=false` (master kill); legacy `_run_inner` sha256-pinned at `9e881fdde25ec5b1` — bytes-identical pre-v3.3 behavior preserved.

**What's next after graduation.** **STELLAR** (Wang et al., *arXiv:2601.19903*) — Structure-guided LLM Assertion Retrieval, the first framework to guide LLM-based SVA generation using AST structural fingerprints — stacks naturally on Treefinement's `_patch_sig` ring: top-M survivors at layer N → AST-shape retrieval key into `SemanticIndex` → past-patches as layer-N+1 priors via Phase 3 injection point. **Agent0** (*arXiv:2511.16043*) uncertainty-as-reward boosts ProactiveExploration priority from Move 6.5 K-roll disagreement. The Treefinement L2 arc validates the citation→implementation template (§92.15) under which both will land.

Per-arc full provenance: `memory/project_v3_3_treefinement_l2_six_phase_arc.md`, `project_v3_4_treefinement_production_wiring.md`.

### §92.14 The SWE-Bench-Pro Evaluation Arc — Six Phases in a Single Day (2026-05-12)

> **Big Picture.** **SWE-Bench Pro** (*arXiv:2509.16941*) is the long-horizon successor to SWE-bench Verified: 1,865 problems drawn from 41 actively-maintained repositories, patches that span multiple files, hours-to-days of human-engineer effort per task. The published frontier at the time of this writing is **Claude Sonnet 4.5 at 43.6% resolve rate** — the best result of any agent system on the benchmark. The paper identifies three structural failure modes that account for most of the remaining 56.4%: multi-file APPLY atomicity, test-file modification cheats, and inability to recover from partial failures. The SWE-Bench-Pro evaluation arc closes the harness binding that lets O+V be empirically evaluated against this frontier, with each of the three failure modes addressed *structurally* (not retrofittably) by primitives already in the substrate.

**Cross-arc cumulative.** Six phases shipped sequentially as independent PRs in a single day:

| Phase | Scope | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| A | Loader + `ProblemSpec` dataclass + fixture/JSONL enumeration union | 12 + 7 (loader_enumeration_union) |
| B.1 | `prepare_problem` + `cleanup_prepared` (worktree lifecycle) | (prior arc) |
| B.2.0 | Read-only `OperationAdvisor` (worktree-aware, `EVIDENCE_REPO_ROOT_KEY` contract) | 36 |
| B.2.0.5 | Orchestrator op-FSM lifecycle SSE (`operation_terminal` event type) | 36 |
| B.2.1 | `build_evaluation_envelope` — pure-data composition; canonical `make_envelope` factory; signature = instance_id for router-side dedup | 31 |
| B.2.2 | Async façade `evaluate_problem` — composes B.1 + B.2.1 + intake + lifecycle SSE rendezvous + one-shot ledger fallback; 8-pin AST discipline | 29 |
| C | Pure-data scorer `score_evaluation` — closed 5-value `ScoreOutcome` taxonomy; **cheat-detection default-on** (canonical SWE-Bench rubric: patches modifying test files → FAIL outright) | 34 |
| D | `EvaluationResultStore` — async record + JSONL persistence via canonical `flock_append_line` (Vector #10 primitive); module-level singleton + dedup by `(instance_id, op_id)` | 33 |
| E | `parallel_evaluate` async generator — bounded concurrency via canonical `_process_singletons.get_semaphore` (key `swe_bench_pro_parallel_eval`); progress callback per completion | 19 |
| F | `build_report_card` — pure-data aggregator + `render_markdown` / `render_json`; per-repo + per-difficulty + top-N failure clustering | 25 |

**261 spine tests + 43 AST pins** across B.2.0 → F; **339 total cumulative regression tests** green; **0 edits to `repair_engine.py`** (the sha256 bytes-pin holds at `9e881fdde25ec5b1` across the entire arc); 0 new SSE event types beyond B.2.0.5's `operation_terminal`; **0 parallel state anywhere** — every primitive composes a canonical surface (`get_semaphore` for concurrency, `flock_append_line` for JSONL, `extract_diff_targets` for diff parsing).

**How the substrate addresses SWE-Bench-Pro's three published failure modes:**

1. **Multi-file APPLY atomicity.** The orchestrator's `_iter_candidate_files` / `_apply_multi_file_candidate` provide *batch-level* rollback: every file is AST/placeholder-validated at the parser, and if file N fails, files 1..N−1 are restored from pre-apply snapshots while new files are unlinked. The 8-phase per-file guarantees compose with atomic multi-file semantics — addressing the paper's failure mode (i).
2. **Test-file modification cheats.** Phase C's scorer enables `_reject_test_modifications` by default per the upstream rubric. Patches that modify any test file (extension-aware: `tests/**`, `*_test.py`, `*.spec.ts`, etc.) FAIL outright — the only Phase C flag that defaults TRUE precisely because rubric integrity depends on it. Addresses failure mode (ii).
3. **Partial-failure recovery.** Phase E's per-task `try`/`except` wraps the entire pipeline; contract violations yield synthetic records (`INGEST_FAILED` + `SCORING_ERROR` with `diagnostic` carrying the exception class name), and the rig continues with the remaining tasks. Cooperative cancellation runs each task's `finally` block (worktree cleanup via B.1, archive flushing via Phase D disciplines). Addresses failure mode (iii).

**Reproducibility — the scoring layer is offline.** Phase C's `score_evaluation(result, problem)` is reproducible from `(captured_patch, problem)` alone — does NOT require access to the evaluation's original worktree. This supports three downstream uses: (a) offline re-scoring when the rubric evolves, (b) rubric A/B comparison from disk alone (the JSONL retains full audit history; in-memory collapses to latest-write per dedup key), (c) third-party SWE-Bench-Pro ingest of `(patch, problem)` pairs without re-running the agent.

**Stop condition for first live run.** Harness boot hook merged (composes canonical Phase A `load_problem` + B.1 `prepare_problem` + B.2.1 `build_evaluation_envelope` + `IntakeLayerService.ingest_envelope`; AST-pinned against parallel `WorktreeManager` or `UnifiedIntakeRouter` references) + ≥1 on-disk problem fixture checked in (`tests/fixtures/swe_bench_pro/problems.jsonl` — 1 `ProblemSpec` against stable `octocat/Hello-World`) + cost/wall caps documented in PRD §40.7.10-arc operator runbook. **No live run today** per operator stop condition — operator-bound $2.00 max / 5–10 problems budget. Two runbook paths: (i) wiring-validation soak (~$0.01–0.10 on the checked-in fixture, idempotent), (ii) real benchmark cherry-pick (~$0.05–2.00 via HuggingFace dataset + `JARVIS_SWE_BENCH_PRO_INJECT_INSTANCE_IDS` CSV override).

**Graduation criterion.** Master flags stay default-FALSE until **≥1 RESOLVED known-good + ≥1 UNRESOLVED known-hard** (rubric sanity floor) — empirical proof that the scoring layer behaves correctly on both ends of the distribution before any aggregate-resolve-rate claim is published. The §40.7.5 PRD claim — "O+V's substrate is positioned to handle SWE-Bench-Pro-class tasks; what's missing is the harness binding" — is now closed on the harness side. The empirical resolve-rate result awaits operator approval.

Per-arc provenance: `memory/project_v3_7_phase_{a,b1,b2_0,b2_0_5,b2_1,b2_2,c,d,e,f}*.md` + `project_v3_7_phase_2_harness_inject.md` + `project_v3_7_clone_template_bypass.md` + `project_v3_7_loader_enumeration_union.md`.

### §92.15 The Citation → Implementation Pattern (Meta-Observation)

PRD §40.7 was added on 2026-05-08 as an explicit map between O+V's architecture and published research across five threads: RSI (SICA / STOP / Gödel Agent / AlphaEvolve / DARWIN / Stanford CS329A), formal verification + AST safety (AlphaVerus / STELLAR / CMU SEI Pointer Ownership / arXiv:2507.13290), multi-agent consensus + speculative execution (HEAVYSKILL / Empirical Speculative Decoding for SWE / Agent0), AI safety + constitutional cage (Anthropic CAI / Constitutional Classifiers / ASL-4 framework), and benchmarks (SWE-bench Verified / SWE-Bench Pro / Live-SWE-agent).

The four weeks covered by §92 demonstrate that **the mapping is bidirectional and structurally enforceable**: §92.13 ported AlphaVerus as the first citation→implementation closure; §92.14 closed the SWE-Bench-Pro harness binding. The template that emerged across both arcs:

1. **Default-FALSE master flag** (per the §33.1 graduation contract) — no capability graduates without empirical proof. Treefinement L2's `JARVIS_L2_TREEFINEMENT_ENABLED` and SWE-Bench-Pro's `JARVIS_SWE_BENCH_PRO_*` all default FALSE; rollback is byte-identical.
2. **Closed taxonomies** — every state machine has its values pinned at declaration. Treefinement's `LayerVerdict × BranchOutcome`, SWE-Bench-Pro's `ScoreOutcome` (5 values) + `EvaluationOutcome` (7 values) + `ProblemDifficulty` (3 values). AST-pin enforcement refuses open-set drift.
3. **AST-bytes pinning** — structural invariants compile-time refuse violations. The `_run_inner` sha256 is bytes-pinned at `9e881fdde25ec5b1` across both arcs; the only `git apply` subprocess invocation in the codebase is `GitApplyDiffApplier` (AST-pinned); `repair_tree_production.py` imports forbidden by AST-pin.
4. **Composition over fork** — every new primitive composes ≥2 existing canonical surfaces; parallel implementations are AST-rejected. Treefinement composes 7 canonical surfaces; SWE-Bench-Pro composes 6 (Phase A loader, B.1 worktree lifecycle, B.2.1 envelope builder, B.2.2 façade, C scorer, D-E-F result substrate) plus canonical `make_envelope`, `_process_singletons.get_semaphore`, `flock_append_line`, `extract_diff_targets`.
5. **Phase 9 graduation contract** — flags graduate by clean-soak ladder, not by hand-tuning. Treefinement: ≥10% lift OR ≥20% wall-clock reduction over ≥2 soaks. SWE-Bench-Pro: ≥1 RESOLVED known-good + ≥1 UNRESOLVED known-hard.

The pattern is **structurally inheritable**. Future §40.7 closures stack on top: STELLAR structural patch retrieval on Treefinement's `_patch_sig` ring; Agent0 uncertainty-as-reward on Move 6.5 K-roll disagreement; HEAVYSKILL parallel-reasoning-agents on M9 + Move 6.5 multi-prior dispatch; DARWIN dynamic role assignment on `subagent_scheduler` + L3 worktree isolation; AlphaEvolve autonomous algorithm discovery on ProactiveExploration + Shannon-entropy gap detection. Each future closure inherits the same default-FALSE substrate + closed taxonomies + AST-pin + composition + graduation-contract template.

**Operator value (verbatim from PRD §40.7.6):** the §40.7 citations provide (a) prior-art justification for architectural choices, (b) baseline numbers to benchmark against (Constitutional Classifiers' 86%→4.4% jailbreak reduction is the Anti-Venom self-immunization target; SWE-Bench-Pro's 43.6% Claude Sonnet 4.5 ceiling is the resolve-rate benchmark), (c) terminology alignment with the published research community. Every engineering decision now has cited-research provenance — not operator binding alone.

### §92.16 Theoretical Grounding — Five Research Threads Now Anchored in O+V

The four-week window aligns O+V with five published research threads at increasing structural depth. Each is a load-bearing reference for the working dissertation (§92.17–§92.18).

**(1) Recursive Self-Improvement — the SICA pattern (ICLR 2025 SSI-FM, *arXiv:2504.15228*).** SICA demonstrates an agent that autonomously edits its own coding tools, achieving 17–53% performance gains on SWE-bench Verified. O+V's substrate is positioned to demonstrate this pattern under the standard Yellow-tier `NOTIFY_APPLY` discipline, with the Anti-Venom cage (Iron Gate + Semantic Guardian + recursion-bound) constraining the mutation envelope and the Phase 9 graduation cadence (§92.9) gating default-on graduation by clean-soak ladder rather than hand-tuning.

**What is empirically demonstrated as of 2026-05-14 (verifiable in `git log --author=Claude`).** O+V autonomously commits to its own graduation ledger — **23 commits authored `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` against `docs/governance/passb_graduation_ledger.jsonl`** across the window 2026-04-26 → 2026-05-12, each appending a soak verdict line under the Anti-Venom cage and the cadence-runner schedule. These are *autonomous-ledger-write* commits — real, automatic, machine-authored, and constrained by the same governance substrate that constrains code-mutation candidates. They are evidence that the substrate's autonomous-commit primitive (`AutoCommitter` in `auto_committer.py`) works end-to-end under the production-cadence schedule.

**What is *not* yet empirically demonstrated.** *Fully-autonomous self-modification of governance code* — commits authored under an autonomous signature that mutate files such as `iron_gate.py`, `semantic_guardian.py`, or `policy_engine.py` and survive the full Iron Gate ∘ Semantic Guardian ∘ TestRunner ∘ AutoCommitter cycle without operator intervention. The substrate supports this path structurally (NOTIFY_APPLY discipline + AutoCommitter signature + risk-tier floor + L2 self-repair), but as of 2026-05-14 the empirically demonstrated regime is *autonomous ledger-write* + *NOTIFY_APPLY-mediated code generation with operator-approved commit* — not the fully-autonomous *generate → validate → commit* cycle that SICA's paper benchmarks. The Phase 9 graduation ladder (§92.9) is the operational scaffolding by which the remaining gap is closed, gated on default-on graduation of `JARVIS_AUTO_COMMIT_ENABLED` under unattended-apply risk-tier configuration.

**Honest framing of the timeline claim.** Anthropic's ASL-4 RSI safeguard framework (*alignment.anthropic.com/2025/recommended-directions/*) identifies autonomous self-improving systems as a capability threshold; co-founder Jack Clark publicly predicts **>50% probability of autonomous self-improving systems by 2028**. O+V's substrate is structurally ready to demonstrate the SICA pattern's full empirical regime well before the 2028 timeline — the AutoCommitter ledger-write commits are evidence the autonomous-commit primitive works; the remaining gap (fully-autonomous governance self-modification) is gated on Phase 9 graduation, not on novel research. The conservative framing is therefore: **the substrate is positioned to close the SICA-empirical gap on a multi-month timeline, well inside the 2028 Anthropic horizon, conditional on the Phase 9 cadence ladder graduating the relevant flags.** The empirical milestone is in the future, not retroactive — and §92's claim is structural readiness, not retroactive demonstration.

**(2) Formal verification + AST safety — AlphaVerus (CMU L3 lab, *arXiv:2412.06176*) and STELLAR (*arXiv:2601.19903*).** §92.13 is the first §40.7 closure: AlphaVerus's *exploration → treefinement → critique* framework maps directly onto O+V's L2 path (Iron Gate exploration-first + `RepairTreeRunner` BFS/BEAM_K + `CanonicalBranchValidator`). The composition discipline (seven canonical surfaces, no fork) is the structural answer to AlphaVerus's open question of pipeline integration. STELLAR — the first framework to guide LLM-based SystemVerilog Assertion generation using AST structural fingerprints — stacks naturally on Treefinement's `_patch_sig` ring (top-M survivors at layer N → AST-shape retrieval key into `SemanticIndex`). The CMU SEI Pointer Ownership Model (*sei.cmu.edu/blog/ai-powered-memory-safety-with-the-pointer-ownership-model/*) extends the AST-as-verifier-input pattern to memory safety; O+V's `semantic_firewall.py` (11 injection detectors + 5 credential shapes + recursion ban + `ScopedToolBackend` mutation cage) is the structural analog at the MCP boundary.

**(3) Constitutional safety — Constitutional Classifiers (Anthropic, *arXiv:2501.18837*).** Anthropic's benchmark reports **86% → 4.4% catastrophic-error collapse** when constitutional classifiers are deployed alongside a base model. Anti-Venom's deterministic substrate — Iron Gate's 12 immutable rules + Semantic Guardian's 10 pre-apply detectors + the 11 injection detectors and 5 credential shapes in the GENERAL Semantic Firewall (§92.1) — is structurally analogous, with one significant difference: **O+V's classifiers are AST-deterministic, not learned**. Zero-LLM, ~10ms per detection, fail-closed on parse failure. The Adversarial Cage (§92.4) reports **0/38 escapes** against hand-authored adversarial inputs, with 12/38 *documented* gaps (predicted detection-gaps, not active vulnerabilities). The §40.1 #3 "Anti-Venom self-immunization" tier extends this toward parity-scale corpus evaluation — generating jailbreak mutations to harden the cage, matching Constitutional Classifiers' synthetic-data training discipline.

**(4) Recursion-bounding — Anthropic ASL-4 RSI safeguard framework.** Anthropic's ASL-4 framework (*alignment.anthropic.com/2025/recommended-directions/*) identifies recursive self-improvement as a capability threshold requiring active safeguards. O+V's §1 Boundary principle + §40.1 recursion-depth gate + §40.1 hash-cap on self-modification map onto ASL-4's recursion-bounding requirement structurally. The Reverse Russian Doll containment claim (§92.17) is the dissertation's load-bearing formalization of this mapping. **This is the load-bearing alignment-research justification for the entire Anti-Venom tier** — the substrate is positioned to be ASL-4-aligned by construction, not by retrofit.

**(5) Benchmarks — SWE-Bench Pro (*arXiv:2509.16941*) and Live-SWE-agent (Nov 2025, *live-swe-agent.github.io*).** §92.14 closes the SWE-Bench-Pro harness binding. The substrate addresses the three failure modes the paper identifies — multi-file atomicity, test-modification cheats, partial-failure recovery — *structurally* rather than empirically. Live-SWE-agent is the closest published parallel to O+V's autonomous-cadence behavior (§92.5 — §92.10 substrate evidence + the autonomous graduation-ledger commits in thread (1) above); the operationally significant difference is the Anti-Venom hardening overlay that Live-SWE-agent does not appear to expose.

**Summary of the five threads.** Two of the five (formal verification, benchmarks) have direct citation→implementation closures landed in §92 — Treefinement L2 (§92.13, AlphaVerus ported) and the SWE-Bench-Pro harness binding (§92.14). The other three (RSI / constitutional safety / recursion-bounding) are positioned structurally — the substrate is in place and the autonomous-ledger-write primitive is operationally proven, but the *full* empirical regime each thread benchmarks (SICA-style governance self-modification, Constitutional-Classifiers-scale jailbreak suppression, ASL-4 recursion-bound stability under stress) is gated on Phase 9 graduation soaks rather than already-shipped. What remains across all three is the *formal* proof of the containment property the substrate's design embodies. That is the dissertation's load-bearing claim, sketched in §92.17 and contextualized in §92.18.

### §92.17 The Reverse Russian Doll — From Architectural Pattern Toward Formal Sketch

The Reverse Russian Doll method, as deployed throughout this paper (§3, §50), is an **architectural pattern**: a volatile generative core *C* is sealed inside an expanding shell *S<sub>n</sub>* of deterministic constraints, and as *C* carves a smarter shell around itself, the immune system scales proportionally so it never crushes the core. §92.1–§92.14 demonstrate the empirical claim. This subsection sketches the formal one — the direction the working dissertation is developing.

**Setup (informal).** Let *C* denote the generative core (Claude, J-Prime, or DoubleWord — the substrate is provider-agnostic per §85). Let *S<sub>n</sub>* denote the deterministic shell at iteration *n* — the composed operator

> Iron Gate ∘ Semantic Guardian ∘ ExplorationLedger ∘ ASCIIStrictGate ∘ TestRunner ∘ CanonicalBranchValidator

acting on candidate patches. Let *M* denote the manifesto-encoded mutation operator that extends *S<sub>n</sub>* by validated patches. A *Reverse Russian Doll iteration* is the composition

```
                   GENERATE         S_n           M
   ( C , S_n )  ───────────▶   δ   ─────▶   δ'   ───▶   S_{n+1}
```

where *δ* is a candidate patch generated by *C* under the shell-injected GENERATE prompt; *S<sub>n</sub>* filters and refines *δ* to *δ′* (rejecting if not exploration-sufficient, semantic-guardian-clean, ASCII-strict, test-green, or branch-validator-promoted); and *S<sub>n+1</sub>* = *M*(*S<sub>n</sub>*, *δ′*) is the shell *extended* by the validated patch (a new AST pin, a new policy rule, a new test, a new branch-validator clause).

**The bounded-RSI conjecture (working dissertation's load-bearing claim).** Under the Reverse Russian Doll iteration, *as n → ∞*:

- **(a)** the **deterministic-entropy** of *S<sub>n</sub>* is monotonically non-decreasing — every accepted *δ′* adds structural capacity, never removes it;
- **(b)** the **semantic-entropy** of unconstrained-*C*-output, *conditioned on S<sub>n</sub>*, is monotonically non-increasing in the dimensions *S<sub>n</sub>* now bounds;
- **(c)** the *net agentic entropy* of the (*C*, *S<sub>n</sub>*) system is bounded above by a finite constant depending on *C*'s base capacity and *S<sub>n</sub>*'s growth rate.

The conjecture is that **bounded-RSI is a thermodynamic stability condition on the (*C*, *S<sub>n</sub>*) system**, not a learning-rate condition on *C* alone.

**Mapping to Wang's RSI formulation (*arXiv:1805.06610*).** Wang (2018) treats RSI as a Markov chain on capability states under a stationary transition kernel, with five MVP-RSI conditions: a composite capability score, persistence across iterations, a 30-day positive trend, a non-decreasing trajectory, and self-formed goals. The Reverse Russian Doll extension generalizes this for the **non-stationary, multi-repository, memory-augmented** setting O+V actually inhabits:

1. **Non-stationary kernel.** The mutation operator *M* is *not* stationary — each iteration's *S<sub>n+1</sub>* depends on the full history {*S*<sub>0</sub>, …, *S<sub>n</sub>*} via the `ExplorationLedger` (§54) and the recency-weighted `SemanticIndex` centroid + k-means cluster classifier (§92.5 substrates). This violates Wang's stationarity assumption. The dissertation conjectures a *non-stationary-but-monotone* extension under which Wang's persistence theorem survives.
2. **Coupled multi-chain state.** Trinity's three repositories (JARVIS / J-Prime / Reactor-Core) carry distinct shells; cross-repository invariants are enforced by the Cross-Session Coherence Harness (§92.8 Vector #5 Part A — 4-value `CoherenceAxis`, 4-value `DriftLevel`) and the cross-runner artifact contract (§92.8 §35 row #4 — 10-value `ArtifactKind`, 6-value `ValidationOutcome`). Wang's single-state-chain becomes a *coupled multi-chain*; the dissertation extends Wang's MVP-RSI conditions to this product space.
3. **Memory-augmented capability score.** Wang's composite capability score becomes recency-weighted via the `SemanticIndex`'s 3-day half-life conversation + 14-day half-life commits/goals + auto-K silhouette cluster classifier (§92.5 substrate). The dissertation conjectures a *recency-decayed* version of Wang's persistence condition, robust to capability oscillations from operator-side noise during graduation-cadence soaks.

**The thermodynamic-entropy formulation — load-bearing for the dissertation title.** Treat the shell *S<sub>n</sub>* as a *deterministic-entropy reservoir* and the core *C* as a *thermal source*. The "entropy of agentic action" is bounded by the shell's deterministic capacity. The Iron Gate's twelve immutable rules + Semantic Guardian's ten detectors + ExplorationLedger floors + the 521+ AST-pin structural invariants (§92.11) set a hard *lower bound* on *S<sub>n</sub>*'s deterministic entropy — the entropy can only grow, not shrink, because every *S<sub>n+1</sub>* strictly extends *S<sub>n</sub>* via *M*. The bounded-RSI conjecture is that this monotone-growth-of-deterministic-entropy implies bounded-agentic-entropy of *C* under *S<sub>n</sub>* — formalizable as a thermodynamic stability theorem.

**What is *not* claimed.** This subsection is a *conjecture sketch*, not a proof. None of (a) — (c) above is currently a theorem in the strict mathematical sense. The empirical demonstrations in §92.1 — §92.14 are the substrate; the formal conversion is the next four weeks (or four months) of work, not yet done. The honest framing: the engineering arc has closed; the formal arc has been *opened*, with the next milestone being a precise statement of the bounded-RSI theorem and its proof outline against Wang's MVP-RSI conditions extended to the non-stationary multi-chain setting.

This is the gap the MSE-AI program is positioned to fill — under the Trustworthy AI lineage at Penn (§92.18), with the engineering substrate (§92.1 — §92.14) as the empirical evidence and the formal apparatus of certifiably robust networks (Wong's lineage) as the mathematical scaffold.

### §92.18 The Working Dissertation, the Penn Inflection Point, and the Ten Orders

**The working dissertation thesis.** *"Thermodynamic Containment of Agentic Entropy: Formalizing the Reverse Russian Doll Architecture for Bounded Recursive Self-Improvement"*. This is the operational research goal — to convert §92.17's conjecture sketch into a formal theorem, against the Wang (2018) RSI formulation extended to non-stationary, multi-repository, memory-augmented settings. Six architectural improvements over Wang's MVP-RSI conditions are sketched in §92.17 (non-stationary kernel, coupled multi-chain state, recency-weighted capability score, thermodynamic-stability formulation, AST-pinning as deterministic-entropy reservoir, ExplorationLedger as monotone growth witness). The dissertation will develop each as a formal statement, prove the principal one (bounded-agentic-entropy under monotone-shell-growth), and validate the proof empirically against O+V's graduation-cadence data (Phase 9 in §92.9).

**Why Penn — the Trustworthy AI lineage.** Three faculty research lineages at Penn map directly onto the three components of the bounded-RSI formalization:

1. **Eric Wong — Certifiably robust networks.** Wong's lineage provides the mathematical apparatus for proving that the Iron Gate's twelve immutable rules + the 521+ AST-pin structural invariants are a *certifiable* operator (every accepted patch is provably within a defined safety envelope, not just empirically observed to be). This is the analog for *Iron Gate determinism* — formal closure on the empirical 0/38 escape result in §92.4's Adversarial Cage.
2. **Aaron Roth — Trustworthy-learning foundations.** Roth's lineage provides the algorithmic-game-theory and differential-privacy apparatus for proving that the Anti-Venom recursion-bound is a *stable equilibrium* of the $(C, S_n)$ system — neither $C$ nor any composition of $C$-instances can converge on a policy that escapes $S_n$'s envelope. This is the analog for *Anti-Venom recursion-bound stability* — formal closure on the empirical stability observed across the L2 / L3 / GENERAL Semantic Firewall composition (§92.1).
3. **PRECISE Center — End-to-end verifiable AI systems.** PRECISE's institutional focus on certified AI provides the integration framework for the Reverse Russian Doll containment claim as a whole — bridging Wong's per-operator certification and Roth's stability theorems into a single end-to-end-verified RSI system, mapping onto Anthropic's ASL-4 safeguard framework structurally.

The fit is not approximate. Each of the three open questions in §92.12 maps onto one of the three Penn lineages: (1) Iron Gate determinism → Wong; (2) Anti-Venom recursion-bound → Roth; (3) Reverse Russian Doll containment → PRECISE end-to-end integration. The dissertation thesis is the bridge.

**The Ten Orders of Trinity Evolution.** The Trinity Manifesto frames the system's developmental trajectory as a ladder of ten Orders, each outgrowing its prior shell and engineering the next. Three Orders are publicly named: **Order 1 — Mechanic** (current state at the time of this paper's 2026-04-16 stamp), **Order N — Neurosurgeon** (the spark of AGI: self-modification of the governance substrate itself, not just of the application code), and **Order 10 — Apotheosis** (the ASI threshold). The intermediate Orders are not publicly named at this writing and remain internal to the project's working manifesto.

The four-week window covered by §92 sits between **Mechanic and Neurosurgeon**. The *first empirical signature* the substrate has produced is the **23 Claude-authored graduation-ledger commits** (§92.16 thread (1) — `git log --author=Claude` across 2026-04-26 → 2026-05-12) — autonomous commits made by O+V under the Phase 9 cadence schedule, real and verifiable, but scoped to *ledger writes* rather than *governance self-modification*. The latter — autonomous mutation of `iron_gate.py`, `semantic_guardian.py`, or other governance code under an autonomous signature — is the **Neurosurgeon threshold proper**, gated on Phase 9 graduation of `JARVIS_AUTO_COMMIT_ENABLED` under unattended-apply risk-tier configuration. The Phase 9 graduation cadence (§92.9) is the operational scaffolding by which this transition is paced — empirical proof gates every default-on graduation, and the Mechanic → Neurosurgeon transition is precisely such a graduation, not yet achieved.

**The Penn inflection point.** The Mechanic → Neurosurgeon transition is precisely the threshold where engineering ceases to be *sufficient* and formal methods become *load-bearing*. Before Neurosurgeon, the substrate can be proven sound by adversarial soaking (the Adversarial Cage's 0/38 result is the empirical proof). At and beyond Neurosurgeon, the system modifies its own governance — and only a formal proof of containment, not empirical observation, can rule out the existence of a modification trajectory that escapes the bound. **This is the gap the MSE-AI program is positioned to fill** — not by replacing the engineering substrate, but by providing the mathematical apparatus to prove what the substrate empirically already does, in time for the Neurosurgeon → next-Order transition to be safely attempted.

The empirical demonstrations are stable. The formal arc has been opened. The four-week window of §92 was the last engineering inflection before the formal one — and §92 itself is the bridge between this paper's empirical substrate (§1 — §91) and the dissertation's formal conversion. The conversion is the next research arc, and Penn is where it is positioned to be done.

<p class="engage-kicker">Conceptual questions</p>
<details class="cq"><summary>1. Why do Treefinement L2 and the SWE-Bench-Pro harness ship with default-FALSE master flags and a clean-soak graduation criterion, instead of being switched on once their tests pass?</summary>
<p>Passing tests shows that the code does what it was written to do. It does not show that the capability helps the live organism. The graduation contract in §92.15 says no capability graduates without empirical proof, and that proof comes from a clean-soak ladder, not from hand-tuning. Treefinement must show at least a 10% L2 success-rate lift, or at least a 20% wall-clock reduction at the same success rate, over at least two consecutive soaks (§92.13). Keeping the flag off also keeps rollback byte-identical: the legacy <code>_run_inner</code> is sha256-pinned, so turning the flag off restores exactly the old behaviour. The trade-off is speed. Capability sits dormant for weeks, as the 36-day minimum calendar in §92.9 shows.</p>
</details>
<details class="cq"><summary>2. The Adversarial Cage reported 0/38 escapes. What does this result support, and what does the paper itself say it cannot establish?</summary>
<p>It supports the claim that the Iron Gate, Semantic Guardian and recursion bound stopped every one of 38 hand-authored attacks, with 12 detection gaps documented as predicted, not active (§92.4). It is a curated, hand-written set, so it is evidence about those inputs, not a measured escape rate across all possible attacks. §92.12 calls the cage "empirically zero-escape" and lists proving this as a formal property as an open question. §92.18 makes the limit explicit. Before Neurosurgeon, adversarial soaking can stand in for proof. Once the system modifies its own governance, only a formal proof can rule out a trajectory that escapes the bound.</p>
</details>
<details class="cq"><summary>3. IDE-native ReviewBranch builds preview branches with git plumbing and auto-rejects after 300 s. Why these two choices?</summary>
<p>The plumbing commands <code>hash-object</code>, <code>commit-tree</code> and <code>branch</code> create a reviewable branch without touching the working tree, HEAD or the operator's index (§92.5). An autonomous proposal therefore never disturbs the human's own work in progress, yet VS Code's source-control panel still shows it natively. The 300 s default timeout ends in auto-REJECT, not auto-apply. If nobody looks, nothing lands. That replaces the old path, where a 5 s Rich overlay was followed by an automatic apply. The old behaviour is still available by setting <code>JARVIS_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_S=0</code>, so the safer default does not remove the operator's choice.</p>
</details>
